name: Org Workspace
description: Clones every repo of a GitHub org into sibling /workspaces folders (persisted across rebuilds via a named volume) and generates or updates a multi-root .code-workspace file. Also self-heals your devcontainer setup.

org.description: GitHub org (or user) to clone repos from. Left empty, detected automatically from the bootstrap repo's own 'origin' remote via 'gh repo view'.

repos.description: Comma-separated explicit list of repo names to clone (e.g. 'typescript,devcontainer,action'). Takes precedence over autoDiscover — set this for a stable, reproducible set that doesn't change if the org's repo list does.

autoDiscover.description: Discover the org's repos automatically. Ignored whenever 'repos' is set ('repos' always wins). 'true' (default): sane defaults (public + private, no forks, no archived). 'false': discover nothing. Or a comma-separated token list to control exactly what's included: 'public', 'private', 'internal', 'fork', 'archived' — e.g. 'public,fork' includes public repos and forks, excluding private/internal/archived.

exclude.description: Comma-separated repo names to never clone or list in the .code-workspace, applied to both 'repos' and autoDiscover results (e.g. 'helpers4.github.io,archive-2019').

generateCodeWorkspace.description: Generate (or update) a VS Code multi-root .code-workspace file listing every sibling repo under /workspaces. If one already exists (e.g. committed to the bootstrap repo), its folders list is merged into rather than replaced — other keys (settings, extensions, launch, ...) are left untouched.

codeWorkspaceName.description: Filename for the generated .code-workspace, written at the bootstrap repo's own root. Left empty, defaults to '<org>.code-workspace'.
